---
title: "Limits and browser behaviour"
output: rmarkdown::html_document
---

For app authors checking browser limits, supported input bindings, theming
and accessibility before release.

## Limits

- For cached, restorable inputs, the close-tab warning is armed as soon as the
  browser reports a changed value, even while the server is busy. Paused trackers
  and `guard_unload = FALSE` are excluded. Markers, badges, tab and click guards
  still follow the server. The browser uses JSON equality; the next server state
  wins, including custom comparisons. Password and file inputs have no
  provisional protection.
- Browsers show their own close or refresh warning, ignore any custom text, and
  may not show it at all if the user has not used the page. Treat it as a
  courtesy, not a guarantee.
- If your app calls `updateTextInput(label = )` or similar, the field marker
  disappears until the next change.
- `discard()` sends the saved values to the browser as JSON. Unusual R objects
  may not come back exactly. A file input cannot get its file back.
- An input inside a `renderUI()` that has not rendered yet is not tracked until
  it appears.

## Restoring inputs

Restoration is tested with these Shiny inputs:

- Text and text area inputs, and numeric inputs.
- Radio buttons, checkboxes and checkbox groups.
- Select inputs with the default selectize binding.
- Date inputs and date ranges.
- Numeric sliders and ranges, date sliders and ranges, and date-time sliders.

`discard()` cannot restore file uploads, password fields or inputs without
a Shiny binding. Missing elements are skipped. Password fields are not tracked.
Discard does not undo writes your app has already made to storage.

## For CSS

These names are stable, so you can style them:

| Selector | What it is |
|---|---|
| `[data-unsaved="true"]` | The container of a changed input |
| `.unsaved-sr` | The hidden "Unsaved change" text for screen readers |
| `.unsaved-badge` | The badge |
| `.unsaved-dialog` | The dialog panel |
| `.unsaved-dialog::backdrop` | The native modal backdrop |

| Custom property | Default |
|---|---|
| `--unsaved-color` | `var(--bs-primary, currentColor)` |
| `--unsaved-dot-size` | `.5em` |
| `--unsaved-outline` | `2px dashed var(--unsaved-color)` |

Set these properties on an ancestor or the changed element. Custom marker and
outline colours must have at least 3:1 contrast against the adjacent background.
Rules use `:where()` so app styles can override them. Changed outputs have a
dashed outline. Native modal dialogs keep the page behind inert and return focus
to the opener when closed. Escape keeps editing, except while saving.

`unsaved_badge(label = c(one = "One edit", other = "{n} edits"))` selects
`one` for a count of one and `other` for larger counts. A single template
still accepts `{n}` and `{s}`. The default class is `badge text-bg-warning`;
set `class` to customise it and `live = FALSE` to omit the live region.

## Accessibility and text

The dialog uses a native modal `dialog` element. Its title and message are
linked for screen readers. Keyboard focus stays in the dialog while it is
open. Buttons stack on narrow screens. Changed fields have hidden
"Unsaved change" text as well as a marker. Radio and checkbox groups receive
a group description or a description on their first input.

Use `unsaved_text()` to change dialog titles, messages and button labels.
The message accepts `{n}` and `{s}`. See [Saving](saving.html) for reason
validation and its screen-reader messages.

Password fields are never tracked. Once reported, a password id stays
excluded for the life of the tracker, even if its widget is removed.
File values can enter a server baseline but never a browser snapshot.
Action buttons, tab selections and the package's own inputs are excluded.
Removed inputs are ignored; returning inputs use their retained baseline.

The package cannot recover a lost session or resolve conflicts between users.
See [Get started](get-started.html) for discard requests and
[Server values and tables](server-values.html) for restoring server values.
